html:
SMTO-SKL-0153 — SMTO can't find a saved GitHub account to use

GUID: ae7c57c2-f4b2-5fe2-ac10-74980c22c496
Slug: github-account-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • To work with GitHub for you, SMTO needs a GitHub account saved in Parameter Store, the page where SMTO keeps saved sign-in details. It found none, or none matching the account named. Nothing was sent to GitHub.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the navigation menu and look for an entry made from the GitHub Account template. SMTO only uses GitHub accounts that are saved in Parameter Store.
  2. If there is none, choose GitHub Account in the template list next to New, select New, fill in your GitHub login, account ID, token type, token and allowed repositories, then select Save. This creates the saved account SMTO was looking for.
  3. If an account is already saved, ask SMTO in the conversation to list your GitHub accounts, then repeat your request using the account name it shows. The request may have named an account that is spelled differently or was renamed.

What success looks like

  • When you ask SMTO to check your GitHub connection, it shows your GitHub login as verified.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste your GitHub token into the chat; keep it only in Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHubProfiles could not resolve a github_account record: the supplied account_ref matches no saved Parameter Store entry, or no GitHub Account profiles exist.

What this means

  • GitHub account reference parsing/lookup cannot find an exact saved account, or no eligible account profiles exist. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • GitHub account reference parsing/lookup cannot find an exact saved account, or no eligible account profiles exist.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact account_ref and supported Parameter Store profile.

How to fix it

  • GitHubProfiles.resolve/account found no github_account record for the canonical account_ref, or Parameter Store holds no github_account profiles. Create one from the GitHub Account template in the Parameter Store editor (/parameter-editor), or pass the exact account_ref returned by github.accounts; never pass a token as a tool argument.
  • Create or select an exact GitHub Account profile in Parameter Store; never paste a token into tool arguments.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account is saved and selected without passing tokens as tool arguments.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
